pr_title: Field selector for Services based on ClusterIP and Type
pr_body:
Implement a field selector for services that allows users to filter by the clusterIP field and the Type.
Use this new field to filter server side headless Services on Kubelet to improve the scalability on environments with large number of Headless Services.



/kind feature


#### What this PR does / why we need it:


Fixes #122394,#77662

```release-note
Services implement a field selector for the ClusterIP and Type fields.
Kubelet uses the fieldselector on Services to avoid watching for Headless Services and reduce the memory consumption.
```

FYI @aojea : In Cluster API we did got bitten by this change in our "upgade to v1.31" tests.

The reasoning TL/DR is that it is because CAPI violates the Kubernetes Version Skew Policy 😄 

A good explanation is at https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/pull/10947#issue-2431972898 , and with that PR in CAPI we now use the alpha kubeadm feature-gate `ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode` for v1.31.

I try to summarise it here again though:

What we are doing in CAPI:

* We have a Cluster with Control Plane node `A` on v1.30 (or multiple ones on v1.30)
* We join a new Control Plane node `B` with v1.31
* We delete the old Control Plane node on v1.30

As long as the old Control Plane `A` is around, and if the kubelet on Control Plane `B` talks to the old kube-apiserver on v1.30 (which is very likely):

* non-static pods have issues to come up (because the kubelet is not able to figure out the e.g. kubernetes service IP)
* this could include `kube-proxy` and `cni` on the new node (and also kind of broke `kubernetes.default.svc` for some parts)
* so these CP nodes got basically unusable apart from `kube-apiserver`, `kube-controller-manager`, `kube-scheduler` and `etcd` as long as Control Plane `A` is around.

It heals itself after all kube-apiserver's are running v1.31.

Just wanted to let you know, all folks violating the skew policy in a similar way might hit the same issue.

cc @neolit123
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80774

> Just wanted to let you know, all folks violating the skew policy in a similar way might hit the same issue.

why the kubelet running in the control plane should go to the loadbalancer instead to the local one?

On the bright side It seems this brings a more solid deployment mode https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125582 :)

When using kubeadm join, pointing to the load balanced control plane endpoint was the only way it was possible before the featuregate in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125582 , except you populate the kubeconfigs on your own.

still not exactly as the kubernetes recommended upgrade sequence does not agree with the immutable node (component-bundles) that CAPI (and kOps) deploys. e.g. it just rolls out apiserver,kcm,scheduler instances at the same time.

I was referring only to the skew problem, I can not judge that part, but IIUIC the disruption problem of that approach will be solved with https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/4355-coordinated-leader-election

issue_context.title: Support skip watch Headless Service in server-side.
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support watch service with field-selector spec.clusterIP!=None to skip headless service in kube-apiserver. And kubelet/kube-proxy can skip watch headless-service in the future.
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/42128207/55a3df12-e70d-4b09-b5a4-a5a6ebff890e)

Now, endpoints will be added labels [service.kubernetes.io/headless](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L518) for headless service  by endpoints-controller,  and kube-proxy will ignore  event for it by label-selector. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L913. But headless service haven't be added label and kube-proxy  still watch for it.

For kubelet, it watch service to add service-env for pods , but it ignores headless service when  build service-env-map(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L549). So kubelet don't need to watch headless service either.

### Why is this needed?

In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes,  when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 10, it can save huge network bandwidth and cpu for kube-apiserver.
comments:
> In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes, when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 1

how many headless Services does that kubeflow task creates?

this falls into that area too

> > In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes, when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 1
> 
> how many headless Services does that kubeflow task creates?

Under steady-state conditions, the cluster maintains 30,000 headless services. During daily new tasks, an additional 10,000 headless services will be created. The number of nodes in the cluster is around 7,000

interesting, I can see lately a lot of consumption of headless Services specially in AI/ML workloads,  instead of labelling Services we can add a field selector on the ClusterIP field, WDYT @wojtek-t @thockin ?

/cc @alculquicondor @ahg-g

Submitted https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122541 , we are already having a selector for PodIP https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/50091/ so I think is ok having a field selector for the clusterIP field, that will bring the benefit of being able to build informers that filter headless services by using ` spec.clusterIP!="None"`
/assign

> Submitted #122541 , we are already having a selector for PodIP #50091 so I think is ok having a field selector for the clusterIP field, that will bring the benefit of being able to build informers that filter headless services by using ` spec.clusterIP!="None"` /assign

@aojea 
We firstly consider support the function  by field-selector for clusterIP,  compared to add label to headless service as we discussed in [#122502](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122502) , the main disadvantages is:

kube-apiserver needs to support field-selector with clusterIP  firstly, and then kubelet/kube-proxy can be updated. Otherwise, clients performing List-watch operations will receive errors like this,  which is not suitable for updating on existing clusters. 
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/42128207/c25d9026-d5bd-4f1f-a31a-b70630039c0b)
When using  the way for adding labels for headless-service,  kube-proxy  does not need to be updated (As it always list-watch with label-selector service.kubernetes.io/headless not exists) .

@aojea  If adding a field-selector  for clusterIP is considered to be ok. I think we can add IndexFields for service spec.clusterIP  as well (such as node metadata.name)，it can reduce events-count converted from kube-apiserver common channel to every cacheWatcher，reduce cpu-usage for kube-apiserver.

> . I think we can add IndexFields for service spec.clusterIP as well (such as node metadata.name)，it can reduce events-count converted from kube-apiserver common channel to every cacheWatcher，reduce cpu-usage for kube-apiserver.

That is on sig-scalability area and better @wojtek-t to decide in that, I can see how Headless services are more used lately in Kubernetes , special fo AI/ML workloads, so I think is a fair request to implement this field selector and allow to filter server side headless service, but I do not know the tradeoffs of using IndexFields

> instead of labelling Services we can add a field selector on the ClusterIP field, WDYT @wojtek-t @thockin ?

+1

I would be ok with adding IndexFields for headless services too [re tradeoff, it adds a bit of memory usage, but it is fairly low - there was a similar thing happening recently in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120778 that has a lot of good analysis done]

> I would be ok with adding IndexFields for headless services too [re tradeoff, it adds a bit of memory usage, but it is fairly low - there was a similar thing happening recently in https://github.com/[/issues/120778](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120778) that has a lot of good analysis done]

I can see that IndexFields implementation is feature gated, I think we can iterate here and go with the fieldselector first and evaluate later the IndexFields addition

The documentation currently says that headless services are labeled. Is this not accurate?
